== Web context recovery for iOS sessions

- iOS sessions now refresh the device web inspector connection as the session starts. A device that has stopped reporting web contexts recovers on its next session, with no manual step on the device.
- This applies to every iOS session that reads a web context, including `appium:autoWebview` setup, Safari automation, and the web portion of the view tree capture.
- Previously, once a device entered this state, every later session on that device failed at setup with `Unable to find any web views`, and rebooting the device was the only way to clear it.
- A connection that breaks during a session stays unavailable for the rest of that session. The next session on that device starts with a working connection.
- Android sessions are unchanged.

== Device passcode

- In manual sessions on iOS devices with a custom numeric passcode, selecting *Power* to lock the screen and selecting it again now unlocks the device automatically. Previously, the device stayed on the lock screen, app installation and other device operations failed, and users had to enter the passcode on the physical device.
- Devices with a 4-digit, 6-digit, or custom alphanumeric passcode continue to unlock automatically.
- On iOS 15.4.1 and 16.7.10, device preparation no longer stalls. Setting a device passcode no longer relaunches the *Settings* app repeatedly, and on-device automation no longer restarts in a loop.

== App installation

- Installing an app during a session no longer leaves a full-size copy of that app in temporary storage on the host machine. Previously, every install wrote a copy that was never removed, so installing a series of different apps consumed host disk space until deviceConnect restarted. Once temporary storage filled, later installs failed with `Failed to install the application on the device` and `No space left on device`.
- Installing an iOS app no longer expands the entire `.ipa` on the host machine to read the app's metadata.
- Installing an app from the Apps repository now uses no additional temporary storage on the host machine. Install behavior is otherwise unchanged on iOS and Android.

[NOTE]
====
Copies left in temporary storage by earlier releases are removed when deviceConnect restarts.
====

[NOTE]
====
On iOS, the first install of an app that Kobiton re-signs still uses temporary storage while re-signing runs. This release does not change that.
====

== Device passcode

- The device passcode is now set after the cleanup policy runs, so devices become available with a passcode after a session ends. Previously, cleanup removed the passcode after it was set, so the next session started on an unlocked device. Devices managed by a mobile device management (MDM) solution then opened to an MDM prompt requiring a passcode.

_Applies to organizations that use passcode mode with a cleanup policy._

== New OS support

NOTE: Before upgrading Mac mini hosts to a new OS version, ensure that all connected iOS and iPadOS devices are running supported OS versions and that a compatible version of Xcode is installed. For details on which macOS and Xcode versions are required, see Apple’s https://developer.apple.com/support/xcode/[compatibility information,window=read-later].

This release adds support for the following:

* macOS 27 for deviceConnect host

iOS and iPadOS devices attached to a Mac mini host running macOS 27 come online and run manual and automated sessions. Devices attached to hosts on earlier supported macOS versions are unaffected.

== AI plugin and MCP

- The MCP tool `listAccessibilityValidations` and the REST endpoint `GET /v2/validations/accessibility` accept a `type` filter that narrows results to one accessibility finding type: `TOUCH_TARGET_SIZE`, `COLOR_CONTRAST`, or `CONTENT_LABELING`. Paging reflects the filter, so `total_items` matches that type's count in the accessibility summary.
- Accessibility findings are lean by default. Each item carries `id`, `command_id`, `type`, `issue_name`, and `standard`. Add the heavier fields with the `include` parameter, which accepts `element`, `metadata`, `screen`, and `screenshot_url`.
- Kobiton generates a screenshot URL only when `include` requests `screenshot_url`.
- An unrecognized `type` or `include` value returns HTTP 400 and names the accepted values.
- `GET /v2/validations`, used by Kobiton Portal, is unchanged and returns the full field set.

== AI plugin and MCP tools

- The `automate` plugin adds the `getAccessibilityValidationsSummary` MCP tool. Pass a session ID to get counts of that session's accessibility issues, broken down by issue type and by issue name, together with the number of commands scanned and the time of the most recent validation.
- The summary returns counts only, so an AI assistant can size a session's accessibility results before retrieving the issues themselves. A single session can hold tens of thousands of issues.
- A session with no accessibility issues returns a total of `0` with empty breakdowns rather than an error.

== Session validations in the Kobiton AI plugin

- The Kobiton AI plugin adds a `listAccessibilityValidations` MCP tool. Ask your AI assistant for a session's accessibility findings and it returns them one page at a time, with a screenshot link for each finding that has one.
- `limit` sets the number of findings per call. It defaults to 10 and is capped at 20. `offset` skips findings you already read. Every response reports `total_items`, so you can tell how many findings the session recorded.
- A session that recorded no accessibility findings returns an empty result instead of an error.
- Kobiton API v2 adds a matching paged endpoint, `GET /v2/validations/accessibility`. It takes `sessionId`, an optional `commandId`, `page`, and `rowsPerPage`, and returns the standard v2 list envelope. `GET /v2/validations` is unchanged.

== Kobiton MCP server

- New: the `automate` MCP plugin adds a `listElementSelectionValidations` tool that returns a session's element-selection validations one page at a time. Each validation covers a test step whose target element resolved to a different element than expected, and carries the test step version's screens, target element, action type, and action data.
- The tool takes a required `sessionId`. `limit` defaults to 10 and is clamped to 20, and `offset` defaults to 0 and maps to a 1-indexed page. A session with no element-selection validations returns `total_items: 0` and an empty `items` array rather than an error.
- New: `GET /v2/validations/element-selection` returns the same validations through the v2 list envelope, filtered by a required `sessionId` and an optional `commandId`. `GET /v2/validations` is unchanged.

== AI plugin and MCP tools

- The Kobiton `automate` plugin adds the `listBlockerValidations` MCP tool, which lists the blocked steps from a session's revisit executions, newest first.

- A session with no blocked steps returns an empty result instead of an error.

== Kobiton AI plugin

- The `listFlexCorrects` MCP tool returns the `flexCorrect` corrections recorded on an automation session. Each item reports the corrected element, the baseline device capabilities, and the matching test step.
- Results are paged. `limit` defaults to 10 and is capped at 20, `offset` starts at 0, and the response reports `total_items` and `total_pages` alongside the requested page. A session with no corrections returns an empty result rather than an error.
- The `GET /v2/validations/flex-correct` endpoint returns the same corrections as a paged list, using `sessionId`, an optional `commandId`, `page`, and `rowsPerPage`. `GET /v2/validations` is unchanged.

== Kobiton MCP server

- New: the `automate` MCP plugin adds a `listResponseTimeValidations` tool that returns a session's response time validations. Each entry covers one command that ran slower than its target response time and reports the command id, the actual response time in milliseconds, and the target response time in milliseconds.
- Results are paged. `limit` defaults to 10 and accepts a maximum of 20, and `offset` defaults to 0. Each response carries the page number, the total page count, and the total item count alongside the returned items.
- A session with no commands over the target returns a total of 0 items and an empty list rather than an error.

== Kobiton MCP server

- New: the `automate` MCP plugin adds a `listCrashValidations` tool that returns the crashes detected in a session, one page at a time. Each item carries the crash time, app package name, command ID, and download URLs for the crash log and screenshot.
- `listCrashValidations` returns 10 crashes per call by default and up to 20. A session with no detected crashes returns an empty result rather than an error.
- The crashes returned match the *Crash* validation shown in Session Explorer for the same session.

== AI plugin and MCP

- AI assistants connected to the Kobiton MCP server can now read a test session's validations one type at a time. Seven new tools cover accessibility, crash, response time, blocker, element selection, and Flex Correct findings: `listAccessibilityValidations`, `listCrashValidations`, `listResponseTimeValidations`, `listBlockerValidations`, `listElementSelectionValidations`, `listFlexCorrects`, and `getAccessibilityValidationsSummary`.
- Each list tool returns at most 20 findings per call, with `page`, `total_pages`, and `total_items` counts. An assistant pages through a large session instead of pulling every finding into context at once.
- `getAccessibilityValidationsSummary` returns a session's accessibility counts by finding type and issue name, with the number of steps scanned and the time of the latest finding. It returns no findings.
- `listAccessibilityValidations` filters by finding type: `TOUCH_TARGET_SIZE`, `COLOR_CONTRAST`, or `CONTENT_LABELING`. Items are lean by default. Request the element, metadata, screen, and screenshot URL fields through the `include` parameter.
- New paged REST endpoints back the tools: `GET /v2/validations/accessibility`, `/crash`, `/response-time`, `/blocker`, `/element-selection`, `/flex-correct`, and `GET /v2/validations/accessibility/summary`. The existing `GET /v2/validations` used by Kobiton Portal is unchanged.

== Reporting

- New: the *Device Utilization* report shows device usage by sessions, testing minutes, and unique users for a date range you select. Organization admins open it from *Reports*, under the *Device* category.
- The report lists device name, custom device name, manufacturer, OS, version, UDID, team, and public or private device type alongside the usage counts, sorted so the most-used devices appear first.
- Filter the report by date range and by public or private devices, and narrow it to a team through the table search box.
